items: Identify Award Letter Details: Find your most recent funding offer letter and locate the specific language describing your stipend, tuition waiver, and any service requirements that determine tax treatment.
Extract Exact Dollar Amounts: Write down the cash stipend amount and the assigned dollar value of your tuition waiver from your official university funding documents for use in your tax calculation.

Confirm Funding Classification: Contact your graduate program coordinator or payroll office and ask exactly how your funding is categorized, whether as fellowship, scholarship, or wages, then record the answer.
Track All Income Streams: List every source of money you receive including stipends, research assistantships, scholarships, and any other compensation, because each may be taxed differently.

Identify Taxable vs. Non-Taxable Portions: Determine which parts of your funding package qualify as taxable wages and which may be excluded as qualified education benefits based on your service requirements.
Calculate Your Taxable Income: Add together your taxable income streams and apply the appropriate federal tax brackets for your filing status to estimate what you owe before deductions.
Know Which Tax Forms to Expect: Determine whether you should receive a W-2 for wages, a 1098-T for tuition payments, or a 1099-NEC for contractor work so you can verify all documents arrive.
Understand Employment Tax Implications: Recognize that wages reported on a W-2 are subject to Social Security and Medicare taxes in addition to income tax, while fellowship income may not be.
Determine Quarterly Payment Requirements: Check whether you need to make quarterly estimated tax payments if your withholding will not cover your expected tax liability to avoid penalties.
Set Aside Money for Taxes: Create a dedicated savings account and regularly deposit a percentage of each stipend, typically 15-25 percent, to cover your estimated tax bill when filing.

Decide on Professional Help: Assess whether your tax situation is straightforward enough to file yourself using software or if your multiple income streams warrant paying a preparer who understands grad student finances.
Keep Organized Records Year-Round: Save all funding letters, pay stubs, and tax documents in one accessible folder throughout the year so you have everything ready when filing season arrives.
